name: Woolly mammoth
intro: Zib! Wrangel Island in the Arctic, about 2000 BCE. While people far away are building pyramids, the last woolly mammoths on Earth are still wandering here!
description: The woolly mammoth was an elephant built for the Ice Age, with a thick coat of shaggy hair, small ears, a short tail and long curved tusks. Herds roamed the "mammoth steppe", a cold, dry grassland that stretched across northern Europe, Asia and North America. As the Ice Age ended about 10,000 years ago, the climate warmed, the grasslands shrank, and human hunters spread; mammoths vanished from the mainland. But a small population survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean until about 4,000 years ago. They became inbred over many generations, and then they were gone too.

facts.diet: Grasses, sedges and other tundra plants
facts.extinct_year: ~2000 BCE (on Wrangel Island; ~10,000 years ago on the mainland)
facts.cause: Warming climate and shrinking grasslands, human hunting; on Wrangel, a small inbred population

habitat.biome: Mammoth steppe and tundra: cold, dry, treeless grassland
habitat.climate: Very cold winters, short cool summers, dry

terrain.value: Cold, dry, treeless grassland and tundra
terrain.why: Herds grazed huge open grasslands where only grasses, sedges and low plants could grow.

temperature.why: Its shaggy coat, fat and small ears were built for freezing Arctic winters.

humidity.why: The mammoth steppe was dry: cold air holds little moisture, and there was little rain or snow.

pressure.why: It roamed lowland plains close to sea level.

hotspots.label: Tundra grass
hotspots.fact: Cold, dry grassland with no trees. Mammoths grazed grasses and sedges all day.

hotspots.label: Snowdrift
hotspots.fact: Snow on the ground in summer! Mammoths had shaggy coats, thick fat and small ears to stay warm.

hotspots.label: Dry wind
hotspots.fact: This icy wind is bone dry: cold air holds very little water, and it rarely rains here.

hotspots.label: Icy shore
hotspots.fact: Wrangel Island is a low, flat island in the Arctic Ocean, close to sea level.

hotspots.label: Curved tusk
hotspots.fact: Mammoth tusks could grow over 3 m long, curving up and inwards. They used them to sweep snow off grass.

hotspots.label: Tuft of fur
hotspots.fact: Long, shaggy hair over a soft woolly undercoat. These are the last mammoths on Earth.

hotspots.label: Old bones
hotspots.fact: On the mainland, mammoths died out about 10,000 years ago. Here they lasted until about 4,000 years ago.
